rows.note: This is the all-purpose noun for a supernatural curse or a wish that harm will come to someone.

example.english: The curse made the villagers afraid to go out at night.
example.traditional: 呢個詛咒搞到啲村民夜晚唔敢出街。
example.jyutping: ni1 go3 zo3 zau3 gaau2 dou2 di1 cyun1 man4 je6 maan5 m4 gam2 ceot1 gaai1

rows.note: Use this for a swear word or vulgar expression, rather than for a supernatural curse.

example.english: They can't help but say a curse word whenever they get angry.
example.traditional: 佢一嬲就忍唔住講粗口。
example.jyutping: keoi5 jat1 nau1 zau6 jan2 m4 zyu6 gong2 cou1 hau2

rows.note: Use this when “curse” means the underlying source or root of serious trouble and misery.

example.english: Corruption is the curse at the root of this city's troubles.
example.traditional: 貪污係呢個城市嘅禍根。
example.jyutping: taam1 wu1 hai6 ni1 go3 sing4 si5 ge3 wo6 gan1
